channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Display Ban Slammed
item.description: Retail visibility is not just advertising; it is how many adult smokers discover that alternatives to cigarettes exist. A display ban may make vaping less visible, but it could also make the lower-risk option harder to notice while combustible tobacco remains familiar through habit, history and availability. The policy question should be practical: does hiding legal vapes help people stop smoking, or does it simply make harm reduction less obvious? Public health gains little from making safer choices harder to see. (Published on October 07, 2026byplanetofthevapes.co.uk)

item.title: She Was Told to Smoke. Then She Was Told to Stop Trying to Quit.
item.description: She was first told to smoke, then judged for needing a way out. That contradiction captures a long public health failure: people were encouraged into cigarettes by culture, marketing and social norms, then later treated as the problem when they struggled to quit. Harm reduction starts from a more humane place. It recognises dependence, history and circumstance, and gives people safer routes away from combustion without turning their past into a moral verdict. (Published on October 07, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: EU Nicotine Consultations: The Value of 120,000 Lived Experiences
item.description: One hundred and twenty thousand lived experiences should be difficult for policymakers to ignore. Behind the EU nicotine consultation are smokers, vapers, pouch users and people who have already changed their risk by moving away from cigarettes. Their evidence is not laboratory data, but it is evidence of how policy works in real life. Europe’s next nicotine framework should listen to those experiences before deciding which products adults are allowed to understand, access or use. (Published on October 07, 2026byclearingtheair.eu)

item.title: When Public Health Declares Itself Innocent
item.description: Public health loses authority when it treats disagreement as a threat rather than a test of its own claims. In nicotine policy, declaring one position beyond challenge can shut out evidence on relative risk, consumer behaviour and the unintended effects of restriction. Confidence is not the same as accountability. Institutions earn trust by showing their reasoning, correcting errors and allowing policy to be questioned when real-world outcomes do not match the promise. (Published on October 07, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: Why “Safer” Matters
item.description: “Safer” is not a loophole in public health; it is the point of harm reduction. For people who cannot or will not stop using nicotine immediately, the difference between burning tobacco and using a lower-risk product can be the difference between continued exposure and meaningful risk reduction. Demanding “safe” before accepting “safer” leaves cigarettes with an advantage they do not deserve. Public health should care about every step that moves people away from the most harmful option. (Published on October 07, 2026bymedium.com)
